findings.claim: ROOT CAUSE candidate: the .pb.zst carries a redundant +180 phi/psi grid column (exact byte-duplicate of -180), making LEU 37x37=1369 bins vs MASTER's 36x36=1296. Per-bin rotamer data (probs+chi) is BIT-IDENTICAL between the two for matching interior and edge bins; both have 9 rotamers/bin and per-bin prob-sum 1.0. So drift is a grid-packaging artifact, not different data, renorm, or filtering.
findings.evidence: PB LEU phi/psi centers = [-180..+180] (37); BIN = [-180..+170] (36, wraps +180 into -180). PB(+180 bin) == PB(-180 bin) byte-identical. Interior bins (-60,-40),(-70,140),(-120,120): probs+chi1+chi2 identical to 4dp. Parity test (load() on rotlib.bin, 36-grid) passes 5/5 within 5e-4, proving the shared find_closest_angle lookup is correct on the 36-grid; only load_pb's 37-grid drifts.

findings.source: drift test with PROXIDE_ROTLIB_PB=pb36 (rebuilt 36x36, +180 wrap removed)
findings.claim: FALSIFIED: the redundant +180 grid column is NOT the drift cause. Removing it leaves drift byte-identical (max 0.223386, median 0.002969, 13 missing). find_closest_angle resolves ±180 ties to -180 idx0, so the +180 dup bin is never uniquely selected (inert).
findings.evidence: pb36 (36x36) drift == original pb (37x37) drift to all printed digits. Remaining suspect: load_pb uses geometry_mode=PRECOMPUTED stored COORDS; probs+chi were verified identical but COORDS were never compared. Contact degree depends on atomic coords (clashes), so pb precomputed coords differing from rotlib.bin coords (e.g., converter used NeRF/Engh-Huber placement vs MASTER's stored Cartesians) would drift contacts with identical chi/prob.

findings.source: Kabsch fit pb-coords vs rotlib.bin coords (RMSD 0.018A, t=-1.458,0.03,0.05) + convert_rotlib.rs:171-174 + place_rotamer rotlib.rs:412
findings.claim: ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED: the converter convert_rotlib.rs builds sidechain coords with N at origin (backbone_n=[0,0,0], backbone_ca=[1.458,0,0]), i.e. an N-origin frame, but place_rotamer applies a CA-origin backbone_frame to the stored coords. Every sidechain is thus mis-placed by +1.458A in x (the N-CA bond) after placement, causing the entire contact-degree drift (max 0.223, 13 missing pairs). Data otherwise identical (per-bin probs/chi match; coords match rotlib.bin to RMSD 0.018A under a rigid re-origin).
findings.evidence: place_rotamer: res_frame=backbone_frame(n,ca,c) [origin=CA], switch_frames(res_frame,identity) applied to stored coords. Converter build frame computed = identity axes translated to CA=(1.458,0,0); correct stored coord = built - (1.458,0,0). Fix: set backbone_ca=[0,0,0] (CA at origin). Residual ~2deg rotation vs MASTER = benign Engh-Huber idealization (#884).

query: Comprehensive system preparation audit for proxide epic #977
Comprehensive system preparation audit: all components, tool coverage matrix, parameter licenses
key_findings: PDBFixer: MIT license, covers missing heavy atoms/H/loops/nonstandard->standard, pH-based protonation (simple rules), no pKa prediction, no SEQRES-gap loop model beyond PDB chain
AMBER tLeap: GPL (AmberTools), adds H at pH 7.4, CYX for disulfides (must declare manually), adds Na+/Cl- ions, solvation boxes, no loop building
Modeller: free-academic only (not OSS), comparative modeling with DOPE/loop refinement, homology-based loop insertion up to 12 residues reliably
Rosetta: free-academic/commercial fee, FastRelax for all-atom relaxation, RosettaRemodel for loop building and insertions, no pKa, no solvation
PROPKa3: LGPL v2.1, empirical heuristic pKa in seconds, gold standard for fast pKa
CHARMM36 ff params: free download from MacKerell lab, no explicit OSS license stated but freely redistributable
AMBER ff14SB/ff19SB params: GPL via AmberTools (free); ff19SB excluded from openmmforcefields due to compatibility
GAFF/GAFF2: GPL via AmberTools, free; covers C/N/O/H/S/P/F/Cl/Br/I
Dunbrack BBDEP2010: free, redistributable with attribution, not OSI-listed
OpenFF Sage/Rosemary: MIT-like permissive, small molecules + protein (BPS2025 paper)
CCD (wwPDB): public domain / CC0 effectively; freely distributed
Engh-Huber 1991/2001: academic papers, parameters embedded in PHENIX/CCP4 which are free for academic; no standalone OSS license
